citations.claim: energy has drifted upward by ~131 by the first violating step, exceeding the allowed tolerance
body 3 reached high speed during the close approach, marking the strong-acceleration regime

counterfactual.change: changed G from 5 to 0.5 with all else identical; weaker gravity removes the large-acceleration integration error and the failure disappears

explanation: With dt=1/30 and G=5 and several ~1.4-separated masses including two 20-mass bodies, accelerations are large. The leapfrog with only 6 substeps cannot resolve the close approach of bodies 3-4 (0.66 apart at step 2): kinetic energy grows faster than potential deepens, so total energy jumps ~131 vs allowed ~107. Lowering G alone removes the violation, confirming an integration-accuracy failure under strong gravity at large dt.
vision_note: Five blue bodies start in a tight central clump. By step 2 the middle body and the larger upper-right body have rushed together until they heavily overlap.
